artifacts.synopsis: The SJC denied most specifications of a complaint filed by TE Herron and others against Central Indiana Presbytery's investigative and suspension procedures, but sustained the complaint on the point that Presbytery improperly denied Herron access to Presbytery minutes while under process. The decision includes extensive discussion of pre-trial BCO 43-1 complaints ('interlocutory appeals') and the proper scope of BCO 31-10 administrative suspensions.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Neal Ganzel appealed his conviction and six-month suspension by Central Florida Presbytery for abuse of spiritual authority and related charges. The SJC unanimously sustained both specifications of error, finding that CFP violated BCO 32-20's one-year statute of limitations for most charges and committed numerous procedural missteps that rendered the disciplinary process significantly flawed and prejudicial, reversing the entire censure.

artifacts.title: Bachmann v. Nashville Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE Bachmann appealed Nashville Presbytery's decision to amend its judicial commission's recommended censure of admonition to indefinite suspension; the SJC sustained the appeal, finding NP violated BCO 15-3 by dividing the question and amending the JC's judgment, and rendered the decision that should have been rendered by restoring the JC's censure of admonition.

artifacts.title: McNeil v. Chesapeake Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC ruled that McNeil's appeal was judicially out of order because he had not submitted to a regular trial, having refused to enter a plea or appear before Chesapeake Presbytery's Judicial Commission, and that his subsequent censure of suspension from the sacraments eliminated his standing to file further complaints against post-censure actions of the court.

artifacts.title: Confusing use of 'admonition' in non-judicial rebuke context

matches.evidence: The CCB cautioned that using 'admonish' and 'admonition' outside their technical judicial-censure meaning in BCO 30 could cause confusion when applied to actions against church officers.

artifacts.title: Informal versus formal admonition and due-process requirements under BCO 27-5

matches.evidence: The CCB distinguished informal admonition (ordinary relational correction) from formal judicial admonition, holding that the paragraph in question did not require BCO 27-5 due process.
